a: Two to three hours for most cars. A three-row, heavy dog hair, or a car that's had a rough year takes longer, and I'll tell you how much longer when I confirm the time, so you can plan the day around it.

q: Do I need to be home while you work?
a: No. If I can reach the car and get into it, you can be at work, asleep or out; plenty of people leave the keys and come back to it done. I turn up with my own power and water, so there's nothing to plug me into and nothing to lend me.

q: How do I pay, and when?
a: Cash, Venmo or Zelle, once the car is done and you've had a look at it. Nothing is due when you book and I don't take a deposit. Cards are the one thing I can't take, so it's worth sorting before I arrive.

q: Do you wash the outside too?
a: No, interiors only. Most places hurry through the inside on the way to the paint, and the inside is the part you actually sit in.

q: What if the car is worse than I described?
a: Then the price moves, and you see the new number in writing before anything is booked. I'd rather have that conversation over a message than in your driveway with the vacuum already running.

q: Do you come to my town?
a: Anywhere in Pierce County: Bonney Lake, Sumner, Puyallup, Tacoma, Orting, Buckley and Enumclaw are the usual ones. If you're a reasonable drive past the county line, ask anyway. It's usually a yes.

q: How soon can you get to me?
a: Send the form and I'll come back within 24 hours with a confirmation and a final price. If you're in a hurry, call instead. I'm on the phone from {hours}, seven days a week, and I can usually tell you on the spot whether a day is open.
